articles.title: Where do the Chargers stand in ESPN’s power index ahead of Week 1?
articles.summary: See where the Los Angeles Chargers stand in ESPN’s football power index ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Chargers ' 2026 season is only a few days away. Soon, they will kick off their 67th season in franchise history, and it is their biggest to date.

A lot of eyes will be on Los Angeles as they have all the tools to make a deep playoff run, something they haven't accomplished in nearly two decades. Nonetheless, all that will be forgotten if they live up to the hype this Fall.

ESPN's latest Football Power Index appears to be high on the Chargers. With the 2026 season kicking off soon, they ESPN's Matt Bowen and Seth Walder ranked the Bolts sixth.

According to the Power Index, entering Week 1, the Chargers have a 66.2% chance to make the playoffs and a 36.1% chance to win the AFC West.

On top of that, their projected wins are set at 9.8 and have the seventh-hardest strength of schedule.

The Chargers certainly don't have it easy entering the 2026 season. While their first two games are "easy" (on paper at least), it will be tough sledding in the middle of the season from Week 3 to 10.

That stretch is a gauntlet, featuring six teams that made the playoffs a season ago. The seventh team in that stretch didn't make the playoffs; that team was the Chiefs.

The Chargers have put themselves in a great position to make some noise this season. While a few question marks remain, particularly at interior offensive line, they believe they are better equipped this season to handle adversity or injuries.

articles.summary: Haaland, que no para de marcar goles con el Manchester City, desveló que se mantuvo en forma durante el verano... ¡cortando leña tal y como le enseñó su padre!

Haaland, que marcó dos goles en el triunfo del Manchester City ante el Oporto, suma 167 goles en 203 partidos con los 'citizens' y ya es el tercer máximo goleador histórico del City. En su carrera Haaland suma 366 goles en 445 partidos repartidos entre sus clubes y la selección de Noruega. Carragher cree que Haaland es capaz de alcanzar los cuatro dígitos en goles antes de finalizar su carrera como jugador: "Simplemente no concibo que Haaland no marque 1.000 goles o que no se convierta en el máximo goleador de todos los tiempos". "Nunca he visto nada igual en cuanto a goles y cifras, y ocurre en cada partido. Pero, como lo hace tan a menudo, no parece algo tan extraordinario", compartió el exfutbolista inglés de 48 años. Jamie Carragher insistió en que "simplemente no veo cómo no va a terminar convirtiéndose en el máximo goleador o logrando la mayor cantidad de goles que jamás hayamos visto a nadie". Para alcanzar los 1.000 goles, Haaland necesitaría marcar 634 tantos más antes de colgar las botas. El diario 'The Sun' calcula que el delantero noruego debería meter 63,4 goles por temporada durante 10 años. Oficialmente Cristiano Ronaldo (41 años) es el máximo goleador de todos los tiempos con 978 goles en su carrera, seguido por los 927 goles de Leo Messi (39 años). A Pelé se le atribuyen 1.284 goles, pero su récord no es oficial. Erlign Haaland ha compartido que sólo ha disfrutado de dos semanas de vacaciones en verano, en las que se ha relajado cortando leña en los terrenos de su mansión de Cheshire. En su canal de YouTube Haaland, que ganó la Champions League en 2023 y acaba su sumar los 300 goles a nivel de clubes, comparte que "aquí es donde ocurre la magia. Aquí es donde corto la leña y la quemo". "Me aporta paz mental; eso es lo que me gusta. Cortar leña, quemarla y relajarme, a solas. Me sienta muy bien, me despeja la mente. Así que esto es lo que hago cuando estoy en casa. Contemplar el fuego es pura paz. Es una de las cosas que más me gusta mirar. La naturaleza es vida", explica. Haaland destaca que "llevo haciéndolo desde que tengo uso de razón" y que "lo hacíamos en mi cabaña en Noruega". El futbolista del Manchester City reveló que empezó a cortar leña gracias a una sabia lección de su padre: "Mi padre me enseñó esto: que la leña te hace entrar en calor varias veces. Primero tienes que talar el árbol, lo que te hace entrar en calor. Luego tienes que trocearla, lo que te hace entrar en calor. Ponerla a secar, lo que te hace entrar en calor. Ir a buscarla y meterla dentro, lo que te hace entrar en calor. Y después, quemarla. Entras en calor seis veces gracias a ese único árbol".

articles.body: El PSG y el Slovan Bratislava arrancan este miércoles 9 de septiembre su participación en la Champions League 2026-27. El conjunto parisino recibe a los eslovacos en el Parc des Princes, en el encuentro correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase de liga de la máxima competición continental. Los parisinos afrontan su estreno como vigentes campeones del torneo, tras haberlo conquistado en las dos últimas ediciones consecutivas. El conjunto francés llega a la cita en un momento irregular, tras haber encadenado varios empates en las últimas jornadas de Ligue 1: Lille 2-2, Rennes 2-2 y Lens 1-0 en sus tres últimos compromisos ligueros. Los de Luis Enrique, que buscan un histórico triplete continental, quieren arrancar con buen pie una nueva aventura europea ante su afición en un Parc des Princes que se prepara para una nueva gran noche de Champions. Enfrente estará un Slovan Bratislava que llega a esta cita tras completar una fase previa en la que eliminó al Mjallby AIF sueco antes de superar también al Celje esloveno para sellar su clasificación a la fase de liga. Los eslovacos, líderes de su liga doméstica, afrontan el partido como claros aspirantes a dar la sorpresa ante uno de los grandes favoritos al título. El partido entre el PSG y el Slovan Bratislava, correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League 2026-27, se disputará hoy miércoles 9 de septiembre, a partir de las 21.00 horas (hora peninsular española). El encuentro tendrá lugar en el Parc des Princes. Desde dos horas antes del partido, la previa y los onces en MARCA.com. A su finalización, la crónica, los vídeos con los goles, las ruedas de prensa y las entrevistas con los protagonistas. El PSG afronta su primera Champions League como vigente bicampeón del torneo, tras haber superado al Arsenal en la final de Budapest la pasada temporada. El conjunto dirigido por Luis Enrique llega al estreno europeo tras un arranque de curso irregular en Ligue 1, con empates ante Lille y Rennes en sus últimas jornadas, aunque con una plantilla de enorme calidad en la que destacan nombres como Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Gonçalo Ramos y Désiré Doué, además de refuerzos veraniegos como Zion Suzuki, Ferran Torres o Mika Godts. El Slovan Bratislava afronta su regreso a la fase de liga de la Champions League con Yaya Touré en el banquillo, quien asumió el cargo tras la marcha de Vladimír Weiss padre para dirigir la selección de Eslovaquia. Los eslovacos, cuartos en su liga doméstica y máximos ganadores de la historia del campeonato local, llegan al estreno europeo tras superar en la previa al Mjallby sueco y al Celje esloveno, con el capitán Andraž Šporar como principal referencia ofensiva. Un equipo tratará de dar la sorpresa ante uno de los grandes favoritos al título.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership preview: Rangers eye second place as Celtic set pace
articles.summary: Rangers host St Mirren, while Celtic travel to Perth to take on St Johnstone in Wednesday's Premiership action.
articles.body:
With the Old Firm in action on Wednesday, the Scottish Premiership table will have a familiar look if Rangers can make it four successive wins.

The Ibrox outfit host St Mirren, while Celtic travel to Perth to take on St Johnstone.

Derek McInnes' side appear to be finding their feet after dropping points in their opening two league outings and falling out of Europe.

Meanwhile, Celtic have a perfect domestic record, bouncing back from a Champions League qualifying trauma in Austria and adding an array of new faces at the end of the transfer window.

The Glasgow rivals meet at Ibrox on Sunday in the quarter-finals of the Premier Sports Cup, so how will they warm up for the first derby of the season?

Rangers find themselves trailing third-placed St Mirren on goal difference, following a bright start from the Paisley side.

Head coach Craig McLeish has earned plaudits for implementing a more fluid style and he was named Premiership manager of the month for August.

"I'm not surprised it's come together so quickly - I get that from the outside it might look like that," McLeish said.

"There's an internal belief about what we're doing and the work we can do on the pitch. It could have been even better and we were close to it being even better."

However, the Buddies have already been to Ibrox this season and were soundly thrashed in the Premier Sports Cup.

James Penrice enjoyed a lively Rangers debut that day, scoring one of five goals and setting up another.

The left-back has started each game since, along with central defenders Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez. While the latter is prone to the odd wobble, a settled defence has provided a platform for the recent upturn in results.

Motherwell rarely threatened at Ibrox on Saturday as Rangers spurned several good opportunities to increase their lead.

That result came after wins over Aberdeen and Falkirk. McInnes says confidence is building while admitting there is still a pressure to succeed.

"I don't think that ever lifts until you've got a trophy in your hand," he said.

"But I do think there's been a good feel about the place. What we have had in recent weeks is just small steps, encouragement, confidence levels."

The loss of Lawrence Shankland to injury just as the striker had found his shooting boots is a blow, so Kevin Kelsy may not have the luxury of easing himself into his new surroundings.

Rangers won the previous two league games against St Mirren by the odd goal but prior to that the visitors had an unbeaten streak of four in this fixture.

Celtic had to work hard for their weekend win in Paisley, with McLeish's team impressive between both boxes but lacking a killer touch.

St Mirren will be without the bite of Paul Nsio, who can't play against his parent club, and that could be telling since Rangers had the run of midfield in that cup tie last month.

Hogh and Tierney close to returns for Celtic

Rangers lose Shankland for up to four months

How much will Celtic miss Asian Games-bound Yang?

Celtic were far from their flowing best on Saturday evening but got the job done after falling behind.

Yang Hyun-jun was the star man, capping an energetic display with the decisive finish, but the winger is now away with South Korea for the Asian Games.

His absence will mean a reshuffle but Martin O'Neill may be reluctant to shift Camilo Duran out wide again after a run of three goals and two assists in three games at centre-forward. If he does, on-loan Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka could make his first start.

Of the six players arriving in the final 48 hours of the window only Mheuka and Oliver Sorensen have been used from the bench so far and it could be that Sebastian Tounekti is the safe choice to replace Yang.

Striker Kasper Hogh and left-back Kieran Tierney are also in contention after brief spells out injured.

The champions can expect to face another side who focus on possession and playing through the phases as St Johnstone hunt a third win on the bounce at McDiarmid Park.

"They want to play football as well and they're committed," O'Neill said of Celtic's next opponents.

"There's a vitality about them which is very encouraging. Not dissimilar in many aspects to what Craig McLeish is doing at St Mirren."

Three of Josh Fowler's four goals have come in Perth, while local lad Taylor Steven caught the eye with his crossing from the right in victory over Hibs.

Centre-backs Cheick Diabate and Zach Mitchell are a no-nonsense pair who will put their heads where it hurts, although Saints are yet to keep a league clean sheet.

Head coach Simo Valakari admits they will need a degree of fortune to continue their impressive home form.

"We need to do our football things so well, then at the same time, we need to earn our luck, because against Celtic, if you want to beat them, you need to be a little bit lucky in some moments," the Finn said.

O'Neill was last in Perth as a manager 25 years ago but you don't have to go back very far for the most recent upset, given a home win over Celtic in April 2025 was among the rare moments of joy in a season that ended in relegation for St Johnstone.

articles.title: Manchester United's squad depth analysed as Gary Neville claims Michael Carrick is under pressure ahead of Champions League return
articles.summary: Manchester United return to the Champions League on Thursday night to face Azerbaijan side Sabah; with a Manchester derby three days later, Michael Carrick may need to utilise his squad; Sky Sports' Callum Bishop analyses if the squad is ready to compete on all fronts
articles.body:
Prophetic words from Gary Neville in the wake of Manchester United's 2-2 draw with Everton. While it may only be September, he's not wrong. Pressure is on Michael Carrick and suddenly, this week already feels season-defining.

When the 2026/27 Premier League fixture list came out, United were deemed to have had the statistically easiest opening six games . Halfway through, they have dropped more points than they have gained.

It only gets tougher from this point on. As Neville rightly points out, United kickstart their Champions League campaign on Thursday night against Azerbaijan champions Sabah, before the first Manchester derby of the season three days later.

Given the nature of the two opponents, you would imagine Carrick will be thinking of rotating on Thursday. That makes it the first time we really see what his squad, rather than his preferred XI, has to offer. But does he have a good enough crop?

The general consensus is that United's business in the transfer market has left them short, with a squad that is unable to cope with three games per week due to an over-reliance on the same names.

According to Transfermarkt , United actually have the second biggest squad in the Premier League. However, the balance of that squad is what creates the problem.

They rank highest with their depth in forward areas. However, they rank eighth in midfield and 10th in defence. Take a deeper look into specialist positions and you find they are ninth in right-back depth and 18th at left-back, a position that is constantly being discussed due to Luke Shaw's injury history.

They can only blame themselves for that problem, mind you. Only Everton and Liverpool have placed less emphasis on investment in their backline than the Red Devils since 2022.

The imbalance is one problem. The other is the gulf in quality between the starting XI and the team after changes are made.

Despite financial restrictions that appear to be imposed within the club, you can't hide from the fact they have the highest net spend of any Premier League side since 2022. Yet, said spending still hasn't built a unit that has genuine competition for places.

Using the Everton game as a lone example, Carrick made his first substitutions in the 70th minute. Below is a breakdown of some of the key changes in data from that point on, and what it would've looked like had it been aligned with United's output in the 70 minutes prior.

Essentially, after the substitutions are made, United's territorial identity shifts. While they play more in the opposition half, it's less meaningful as they aren't finding passes in the final third and there is a decrease in chances created.

They are also getting less involved in duels, therefore inviting pressure on themselves and conceding far more opportunities. Now, granted, you do have to take into account the context of the situation. Everton are chasing the game. It's unlikely to pan out exactly the same over the final 20 minutes as it is in the first 70.

However, it highlights that when Carrick turns to his fringe players, they aren't producing enough for him. The exception is clearly Benjamin Sesko, but one impact sub does not translate to sufficient squad depth.

It's not just against Everton this trend is apparent. You can also see it against Hull.

You may look at that data and think 'but United have actually improved after they made substitutions.' However, four of the starting XI against the Tigers were dropped in the next two games, with Carrick having to utilise his squad in the opener due to players still building up their fitness. The changes he made brought the team closer to the XI that would be picked to face Ipswich and Everton.

Therein lies the problem. Even if Carrick changes fewer than 50 per cent of his team, a drop off in performance arises. The players in question responsible have no choice but to step up or leave Carrick vulnerable this week - and perhaps for the season.

If you're someone like Leny Yoro, Patrick Dorgu, Andrey Santos or Joshua Zirkzee, Thursday night should present the golden opportunity to show your value within the squad.

Of course, all of them would want to play in the derby, but getting the European campaign off on the right foot is a must. The pressure on them to deliver if chosen is as great as it will be on the starting core who will no doubt be picked against City.

Neville spoke about Carrick needing to earn the trust of the fans. So do those aforementioned players. Win in the Champions League and you can put some minds at rest. Fail to deliver and the angst around Old Trafford will only grow.

articles.title: Erling Haaland: Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City striker will be greatest goalscorer of all time
articles.summary: Erling Haaland scores double in Man City's win at Porto in Champions League; Haaland has now hit 364 goals for top-flight clubs and country in his 424-game career; Jamie Carragher tells CBS Sports: "I just can't see Haaland not scoring 1,000 goals or being the best goalscorer of all time"
articles.body:
Haaland's brace in Portugal saw him become Man City's third-highest goalscorer of all time, taking his tally to 167 in just 203 appearances, and he is now 93 goals behind record-holder Sergio Aguero.

The 26-year-old has hit 364 goals for top-flight clubs and country in his 424-game career - and Carragher has backed the Norway international to become a record-breaker.

He told CBS Sports : "I just can't see Haaland not scoring 1,000 goals or being the best goalscorer of all time.

"I've never seen anything like it in terms of goals and numbers, and it is every game - but because he does it so often, it does not feel that big.

"He has just scored two goals away from home in the Champions League - any other striker does that; it is an amazing night. It just feels like a normal night. "I just can't see how he does not end up being the greatest goalscorer or getting the most goals we have ever seen anybody get."

Haaland has scored 42 goals in 39 appearances in the group stage/league phase of the Champions League, the most of any player since his first season in the competition in 2019-20.

Porto boss Francesco Farioli described Haaland as a "monster" at his post-match press conference.

Haaland needs one goal to become Man City's all-time top Champions League scorer after equalling Aguero's record of 36 goals.

Haaland has scored 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances but will now turn his attention to the Premier League, where City go to rivals Manchester United on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

Merson: Haaland can score 1,000 goals if he stays at Man City

"The problem is, the older you get, the lesser team you're going to play for. The lesser team you play for, that means they've got fewer better players. If they haven't got better players, you're not going to score as many goals.

"He would have to play at the top with top, top players for a long, long time. But he's a machine. A thousand goals? That'll be hard because he's got to stay hungry at the same time. He's been around a while already.

"You're talking about another six, seven years at the top level. It takes its toll in the end. There are a lot of injuries. But if you said to me he's going to stay at Man City for the next seven, eight years, then I think, yeah, who knows? He could do it."

Haaland: I could've scored more in Porto win

Haaland has hit five goals in five appearances across all competitions under new boss Enzo Maresca - but the ex-Borussia Dortmund forward felt he could have scored more against Porto.

He told Amazon Prime : "Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a difficult fight, man against man. They're a top team, impressive, all of them. They play amazing football.

"Well done to them. But with all the pressure, we have to deliver on the biggest stage. That's what we did tonight.

"Honestly, we controlled the whole first half. Of course, it's a bit uncomfortable when they come high. But we created a lot of chances. I could have easily had a few more goals.

"But second half, we scored and they managed to push us for a good 25 minutes. We managed to hold through and finish the game.

"These are the games we have to win. We had a great start to the season, and in the Champions League, you have to win games. If not, you get all the pressure."

Carragher believes Haaland could become the greatest goalscorer of all time, and the numbers suggest reaching 1,000 career goals is plausible.

At 26 years and 49 days old, Haaland has already scored 364 senior goals. At the same age, Lionel Messi had 348 and Cristiano Ronaldo 219, meaning Haaland is 16 goals ahead of Messi and a remarkable 145 clear of Ronaldo at the same stage of their careers.

Haaland still needs another 636 goals to reach four figures, but his recent scoring rate puts the milestone within range.

Since joining Manchester City in 2022, he has averaged around 51 goals per year for club and country. Maintaining that rate would take him to 1,000 at around 38 years and eight months - although matching Ronaldo's extraordinary longevity would be just as important as maintaining his prolific scoring rate.

articles.title: Ethan Mbappé: "La derrota ante el Betis es enteramente culpa mía"
articles.standfirst: El joven futbolista del Lille asumió toda la responsabilidad de la derrota frente al Real Betis y pidió disculpas públicamente tras una acción que le costó la expulsión
articles.summary: El joven futbolista del Lille asumió toda la responsabilidad de la derrota frente al Real Betis y pidió disculpas públicamente tras una acción que le costó la expulsión
articles.body: Ethan Mbappé fue uno de los protagonistas de la primera jornada de la Champions League aunque por motivos muy distintos a los que hubiera deseado. El centrocampista ofensivo del Lille publicó un mensaje en redes sociales para disculparse después de ver la primera tarjeta roja de su carrera durante la derrota de su equipo por 2-3 frente al Real Betis. "Quiero disculparme con mis compañeros, el cuerpo técnico y los aficionados por esta acción inaceptable. La derrota es enteramente culpa mía y asumo toda la responsabilidad", escribió el hermano pequeño de Kylian Mbappé. La expulsión llegó en uno de los momentos más delicados del encuentro. El Lille había comenzado bien el partido e incluso se adelantó gracias a un gol de Ayase Ueda tras una asistencia del propio Ethan Mbappé. Sin embargo, el conjunto francés vio cómo el Betis remontaba en el inicio de la segunda mitad hasta colocarse con un 2-3 a favor. Fue entonces cuando se produjo la acción que cambió definitivamente el encuentro. En el minuto 55-56, Ethan mantuvo un intercambio con el defensa bético Natan. Según diversas informaciones, el brasileño provocó verbalmente al jugador francés después del tercer gol verdiblanco. Mbappé perdió los nervios y respondió con un codazo o golpe con el brazo al rostro del central del Betis. El árbitro Georgi Kabakov no apreció inicialmente la agresión, pero fue advertido por el VAR para revisar la jugada en el monitor. Tras observar las imágenes, el colegiado decidió mostrar la tarjeta roja directa a Ethan Mbappé por conducta violenta. Natan también fue amonestado con tarjeta amarilla por su participación en el incidente, pero la sanción más severa recayó sobre el futbolista del Lille, que dejó a su equipo con 10 jugadores durante la recta final del choque. Con inferioridad numérica, el conjunto dirigido por Davide Ancelotti fue incapaz de reaccionar y terminó cayendo ante el Betis. Consciente de que su expulsión condicionó las opciones de remontada de los franceses, Ethan no buscó excusas y asumió toda la culpa del resultado. "Dejé a mis compañeros en una situación difícil en la competición más importante. Lo siento", reconoció el joven jugador de 19 años, en un gesto de autocrítica que ha marcado el día después de una noche para olvidar en Lille.

articles.title: Guruzeta repite ausencia y Terzic llama a entrenar a Igor Oyono
articles.standfirst: El Athletic fichó al delantero del Villarreal, que decidió romper relaciones con el club rojiblanco
articles.summary: El Athletic fichó al delantero del Villarreal, que decidió romper relaciones con el club rojiblanco
articles.body: Edin Terzic mira al filial para preparar el partido del sábado ante el Elche, primero de una semana que tendrá otros dos encuentros ante Levante y Alavés. La ausencia de Guruzeta, que no ha entrenado por segundo día consecutivo, ha llevado al técnico a citar al joven Igor Oyono, delantero de 18 años que desempeña en el Bilbao Athletic y que llegó al club en 2024 procedente del Villarreal tras una operación por la que el conjunto castellonense mostró gran enfado y rompió relaciones con el club rojiblanco. El técnico alemán ha reclutado desde el filial para el entrenamiento de este miércoles a los habituales Monreal y Selton, que el domingo tuvieron minutos frente al Avilés después de haber estado convocados con el primer equipo ante el Atlético, Larrea -central, igual que Monreal-, y a Oyono. Terzic siguió en directo el último encuentro del filial y en el mismo Oyono entró al campo en el minuto 58. Internacional en categorías inferiores, Oyono se incorporó al Athletic en febrero de 2024, todavía sin cumplir los 16 años de edad. El Villarreal, su club de procedencia, consideró una maniobra invasiva el fichaje y su presidente no acudió al palco en el siguiente partido de San Mamés. Nacido en Barakaldo, el chico fue fichado por el Villarreal desde la escuela formativa fabril y por la misma vía de fichaje como menor de edad salió de Castellón. El pique fue grande porque el Villarreal demoró los trámites del traspaso, no permitiendo el inmediato debut del futbolista. La citación de Oyono es un refuerzo de Terzic y su cuerpo técnico hacia el trabajo desempeñado en las categorías inferiores, aunque no quiere decir que vaya a tener presencia en la convocatoria ante el Elche porque hay confianza en que Guruzeta entrene el jueves y esté disponible. De momento, eso sí, el entrenador quiere transmitir a Oyono que le tiene bien presente en el radar.

articles.title: Rhys Carr interview: Former Coventry assistant manager on 'Premier League attributes' in the squad as he seeks next challenge
articles.summary: Former Coventry City caretaker manager Rhys Carr opens up on his exit from the club in this exclusive interview with Sky Sports; Carr shares what he learned coaching women, why he believes individual coaching is so important, and his long-term plan to be a head coach
articles.body:
He worked as an individual coach at Bristol City, Wolves and Sheffield United at a time when the role was still rare. He has just finished the League Managers' Association diploma in football management. "Probably the best course that I have done," he says.

He still runs his own coaching conferences, in fact, with another lined up at Brentford's stadium after three years hosting events at St George's Park. Big names sharing their experiences. "It is like the Wizard of Oz, pull the curtain back and it is just me," he jokes.

There was his time as assistant manager of Republic of Ireland's women's team. "It was only a handful of games but I learned loads about communication. I am probably a better husband because of it. All of a sudden, I was learning from 30 different women."

While his recent roles have been as an assistant manager, he is ambitious. "I want to be a head coach," he tells Sky Sports . That taste of it at Coventry has whet the appetite. "It has made me even hungrier." But, at 39, time is on his side. He is open to anything.

There is nothing but praise for Coventry. "The fans are incredible. They surpassed what I thought they were going to be. There are unbelievable people at the football club." There is admiration for Mark Robins too. "One of the best in terms of giving you a purpose."

But perhaps the clues that it would not be a stable environment were there on day one. Robins' long-time assistant Adi Viveash departed. "It was on my first day that I was told that the club had parted company with Adi. The whole training ground was in shock."

By November, Robins' seven-year-spell in charge was over and Carr found himself being asked to take over the team on a temporary basis. "I was shocked by the decision and had a real sense of duty to Mark. But I needed to work too," he explains. It was tough.

"I wanted to be really authentic. I would hate to have been the type of coach who had been supporting Mark and then did something totally different when it was my turn. You would come across as a fraud then because why had you not been saying this before?"

Carr oversaw three games. "The toughest games you could have had." There was a draw at Sunderland and at home to Sheffield United before being beaten at Burnley. The Blades were second at the time. Sunderland and Burnley would go on to be promoted.

"It was a brilliant experience," he admits. "It is exciting being able to put what is in your head and your ideas out onto the pitch so that people can kind of see it and showcase it. But then, it is quite daunting as well. It might go wrong and then it falls back on you."

It was not too long before Lampard wanted to bring in his own staff. "We had a good conversation. It was frustrating in a personal sense, but there is no ill feeling. That is what happens in football." But Coventry's subsequent success is a what-if moment.

"I sent Frank a message when they got promoted. Would I have loved to have still been a part of that? Yes, of course. And it is a credit to the club's recruitment over the years that there were so many Premier League attributes there just waiting to be unleashed."

Carr worked with many of them. He picks out players like Jack Rudoni, Milan van Ewijk and Bobby Thomas. There is praise for Victor Torp. "His ceiling is really high. He is going to be such a good player. The development of the group has not been a surprise."

That development work has been the focus for much of his coaching career, simply trying to make players better. "That was one of the remits when I went in. Because of my background, it was to ensure every player had their own individual development plan."

He explains: "If kids of nine have that now then why would that support fall away in the first team when the challenge is at its highest? You do not want to create robots, you want to give them solutions. We look at their super strengths. Why were they signed?"

A lot of it is common sense. "If it is centre-backs you want them winning first contacts and building attacks. If it is your eights and 10s, you want them receiving between the lines, creating opportunities for others and chipping in with goals of their own."

Working with someone like Rudoni, the former Wimbledon youth player who made his Premier League debut on the opening day of the season against Arsenal, was particularly rewarding. "Jack was so articulate when discussing his plan," says Carr.

"No disrespect to the lower levels, but he would have to come searching for the ball there. Part of the challenge with Jack at the time was working with him to have the patience to stay in position, because these good players will now find you with the ball.

"That way, when you get it in that position, you are now in a place where you can hurt the opposition, because you are off the back of their midfield, you can slide through for assists, you can get your own shots off, you can create and you can score goals.

"Then, we could look at the bits to brush up on. How smooth can you be when receiving the ball, how quickly can you move from the back foot, hips open, face forward and find quality with the pass. It is about creating more moments to showcase their skill."

But in terms of personal satisfaction, it is a moment with Niclas Eliasson, the Swedish winger, that stands out. "He was a bit like Eden Hazard in terms of his dribbling style. He would keep it close until the defender had a nibble and then shift it," says Carr.

"I remember working with him and we saw that an opposition full-back liked to lunge in a little bit. He went and worked on it, getting that little half yard, and he scored. He slid over the dugout because it was literally exactly what we had rehearsed the day before.

"And that is all credit to him, none to me at all. He had to do the action. But it is all about the buzz in that moment that you get from working with someone on such a detailed element. The action might only come up once in six games but it did and he nailed it."

Listening to Carr talk about these one-on-one sessions, it is evident he is still chasing that buzz. He knows that his next chance is unlikely to be a firefighting role. "I don't have the reputation for that project." But developing players? "That is my skillset."

He wants to set a team up. "I have a 50-page document on it." And has knowledge beyond his years too. "Almost 500 games in the technical area of senior teams." Young but experienced, Carr is eager for that chance now. "I am just itching to get going again."

articles.title: Marlaska abre expediente por falta grave a los policías por su actuación antes del Barça - Elche
articles.standfirst: Portar un símbolo absolutamente legítimo como es la senyera estelada no justifica la actuación policial, ha manifestado el ministro de Interior
articles.summary: Portar un símbolo absolutamente legítimo como es la senyera estelada no justifica la actuación policial, ha manifestado el ministro de Interior
articles.body: El ministro de Interior, Fernando Grande Marlaska, ha avanzado este miércoles que se ha abierto un expediente por "supuesta falta muy grave o grave" a los agentes que golpearon a un seguidor del Barcelona al que arrebataron una bandera estelada antes del partido entre este equipo y el Elche el pasado 23 de agosto. Tras abrir una investigación de oficio sobre lo ocurrido, Marlaska ha señalado en la sesión de control al Gobierno en el Congreso, y en respuesta a la diputada de Junts Marta Madrenas, que de esa "información reservada" se ha pasado a la apertura de un expediente para evaluar si la actuación es constitutiva de falta grave o muy grave. Una decisión adoptada después de considerar que "no se justifica en modo alguno" la actuación policial, independientemente de que esa persona portara un símbolo "absolutamente legítimo" como es la senyera estelada. Los hechos investigados tuvieron lugar el pasado 23 de agosto a raíz de un vídeo difundido en redes sociales que muestra cómo agentes de la Policía Nacional golpean a un joven tras arrebatarle una estelada. El joven se encara con los policías, y estos terminan golpeándole en el suelo. La diputada de Junts ha denunciado que este pasado domingo en Alcorcón (Madrid) se vivió un incidente similar también con un estelada, un episodio que el ministro ha señalado que hay que "contextualizar" pero que, según las noticias que él tiene, sus circunstancias "son absolutamente diferentes y distintas a lo de Elche".

articles.title: Is JJ Gabriel, 15, ready to become Man Utd's youngest ever player?
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old JJ Gabriel has scored two magnificent goals in two Premier League 2 appearances for Manchester United - is he ready to make his senior debut
articles.body:
When Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick was asked about 15-year-old JJ Gabriel last month, he navigated the narrow path between high praise for a young player of immense talent and the knowledge he will ultimately be the one who decides when it is time for first-team exposure.

"JJ is one of the boys," he said. "He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time.

"He's physically adapting to each step, and we're just continuing his development."

Carrick was at Leigh Sports Village four days earlier when Gabriel, making his Premier League 2 debut against Ipswich, ran on to Jack Fletcher's through ball and after taking the pace off the pass with his left foot, scooped the ball over an advancing keeper from the edge of the area with his right.

It was an audacious finish, one that highlighted Gabriel's thought process given the most obvious route to goal was either a low shot or sprinting round the keeper.

Seven days later, against Leicester, Gabriel followed up with a completely different, but even better effort.

Taking Tynan Thompson's short pass in a central position, with his back to goal just inside the area, Gabriel's first touch was a drag back with his left foot that allowed him to spin round so he was facing the right way.

Then, showing strength to keep his balance after being nudged by an opponent, he nicked the ball to his left with his right foot, gliding past a second defender.

He took another touch to steady himself before rifling a low shot into the net from just inside the six-yard box.

From start to finish the manoeuvre took less than five seconds.

It was impossible not to be impressed. The goal itself has been viewed on various social media accounts millions of times.

'Sometimes it gets to a point where you can't not pick him'

Ryan Giggs, United's record appearance holder, was 17 when he made his United debut in 1991.

Like Carrick with Gabriel, Sir Alex Ferguson saw Giggs playing youth football in the flesh, initially in a trial game at the Cliff training ground.

In his first autobiography, Managing My Life, he recounts the experience like this:

"A gold miner who has searched every part of the river or mountain and then suddenly finds himself staring at a nugget could not feel more exhilaration than I did watching Giggs that day.

"I shall always remember my first sight of him, floating over the pitch so effortlessly you would have sworn his feet weren't touching the ground. He carried his head high and looked as relaxed and natural on the park as a dog chasing a piece of silver paper in the wind."

Giggs can't assess what he looked like. But he knows what it felt like and in an insightful chat with his former United team-mate on Rio Ferdinand Presents: The Debrief, , external Giggs offered this assessment:

"Sometimes you have to be patient. Sometimes it gets to a point where you can't not pick him and not have him train in the first team; that might be in a month, might be six months, might be a year.

"It's that in-between time where he thinks he should be in the first team. He thinks he should be in the squad every week when Michael sees it a different way, that, actually, no, you need to play games because it's not really going to do you any good travelling here, there and everywhere and you're getting five minutes here, 10 minutes there."

It feels as though Gabriel is at that 'in-between' point Giggs mentions just now.

Aside from the first game in Helsinki, the forward was a feature of all United's pre-season trips this summer.

Yet he played just once, as a late substitute against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm when his first involvement led to him being clattered from behind by Uruguay skipper Jose Maria Gimenez, who, at 31, is twice Gabriel's age.

United have posted plenty of footage of Gabriel training with the first team this season and having a joke with fellow forward Benjamin Sesko. As Carrick says, the youngster is "one of the boys".

There was a view Gabriel may be given his first-team debut in the EFL Cup third round, which would make him Manchester United's youngest ever player, beating goalkeeper David Gaskell, who was 16 years and 19 days when he made his senior bow. Gabriel is not 16 until 6 October.

However, as United have had a tricky start to the season results wise, and play Premier League opposition in Brighton at Old Trafford on 16 September, is that practical?

Champions League games offer 11 substitute places, rather than nine in domestic competition. Does that mean he could be involved against Sabah FK on Thursday? Given he did not train with the first team on Wednesday, possibly not.

Is the Under-19 Uefa Youth League - a competition United's academy is prioritising after pulling out of the EFL Trophy and National League Cup this season, and for which last season's FA Youth Cup final squad are eligible - a more appropriate stage?

Gabriel would have been looking to a Premier League 2 Manchester derby at City on Saturday evening, but that game has been postponed because of United's various Thursday European commitments.

Thirty-five years ago, Giggs was content when Ferguson blocked media from talking to him.

There was no social media or digital forums. Expectation, discussion and demands now are huge and cannot be silenced.

Those close to Gabriel clearly have their own idea of what his future should look like.

United's last Premier League 2 game before the international break is against Brentford at Leigh on 18 September. After that, England's various age group teams have their matches to play.

Gabriel's own abilities are creating the pathway. The big question is, where does it lead?

articles.title: Top 12 Breakout Stars After Week 1 of the 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: Every year, college football gives us a new crop of superstars who become household names in a hurry.
articles.body:
Every year, college football gives us a new crop of superstars who become household names in a hurry.

Week 1 may have given us a snapshot of some guys we should get used to.

From a trio of defensive playmakers to some new-name quarterbacks to guys who are thriving in new environments, players from almost every position rose to the forefront – including some in the weekend's biggest games.

For this list, we focused on players who posted big numbers in key positions, trying not to give any weight to guys who mopped up in garbage time. No team was represented more than once. We believe those who made the list have staying power throughout the season.

Here are a dozen players who showed out in the full opening weekend.

Deuce Alexander, Ole Miss Rebels Wide Receiver

Those in Oxford, Mississippi, know Deuce Alexander very well. He was a big-time producer a season ago for the Ole Miss team that went deep in the College Football Playoff.

With Harrison "Tre" Wallace III and De'Zhaun Stribling starring, Alexander's 684 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns were overlooked. He was, at best, Trinidad Chambliss' third option.

If a porous Rebels defense continues to rear its head, coach Pete Golding is going to need the same wide-open attack as a season ago. Alexander is the surest thing on the offense besides running back Kewan Lacy.

In a tit-for-tat grudge match opener against Louisville, Alexander's separation was a difference-maker. He's going to be one of the most valuable players in the nation.

Faizon Brandon, Tennessee Volunteers Quarterback

Tennessee really had two players who belonged on this list, but true freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon's historic performance against Furman was just too much to ignore.

He was brilliant against the FCS Paladins after a slow start, throwing for 226 yards and a trio of scores while rushing for 68 more and two additional touchdowns. He showed zip on the ball, a command of the offense and elusive athleticism when plays broke down.

The competition ramps up considerably this week as the Vols go on the road to face Georgia Tech, but the moment in Week 1 wasn't too big for the 18-year-old freshman.

Junior defensive tackle and Penn State transfer Xavier Gilliam's three-sack, five tackle-for-loss performance easily could have made the list, too.

JJ Buchanan, Michigan Wolverines Wide Receiver

There was no bigger (or more controversial) play in Week 1 – or perhaps, the future may tell – the entire season than JJ Buchanan's second last-second Hail Mary reception to help Michigan avoid an improbable upset attempt by Western Michigan in the Big House.

The 6'4", 218-pound sophomore transfer wowed everybody throughout fall camp after following Kyle Whittingham to Ann Arbor. That carried over when the Wolverines needed him most.

Everybody in the stadium knew the high-leaping Buchanan was Bryce Underwood's target both times he threw deep, but Buchanan still went up and made the play to give Michigan a 13-12 win. Dude just made plays all night, though.

He wound up with six grabs for 126 yards and a touchdown on a night when Michigan couldn't muster any offense against the Broncos. He's a star who every team will scheme against.

New report on ex-pros joining LSU's roster

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

Mason Heinschel, Pittsburgh Panthers Quarterback

Mason Heintschel didn't come out of nowhere.

The trajectory of Pittsburgh's college football program changed last year when the then-freshman signal-caller took the field and unlocked the full potential of coordinator Kade Bell's explosive scheme.

He wound up completing 64 percent of his passes for 2,354 yards, 16 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Still, on a national scale, he went pretty much uncharted.

That's not going to be the case this year as a sophomore.

In the season opener against Miami (Ohio), he was nearly flawless in a 59-14 win, completing 31-of-41 passes for 453 yards and tying a school record with seven touchdowns against zero interceptions.

The 6'4", 215-pound youngster is a budding star who is going to put his hometown of Oregon, Ohio, on the map. The Panthers are a threat in the ACC because of Heintschel's explosive arm.

Lincoln Kienholz, Louisville Cardinals Quarterback

Like a lot of elite high school athletes, the lure of playing bright-lights football at Ohio State was a luminous lure for quarterback Lincoln Kienholz three years ago.

The all-world North Dakota prep star signed with the Buckeyes after thinking he'd play for Kalen DeBoer at Washington. But after three years in Columbus, he simply couldn't crack the deeply talented depth chart, causing him to transfer.

Now at Louisville, it appears the next two years could be fun to watch Kienholz play for coach Jeff Brohm.

In a losing effort Sunday night, Kienholz made sure the Cardinals traded punches with Ole Miss after a sluggish start, completing 18-of-29 passes for 301 yards and a pair of touchdowns and running 14 times for 69 more and another score.

He was at his best in the brightest moments, as you could see the third-year junior's confidence growing before our eyes. He's going to be a good one.

Lamont Lester Jr., Colorado Buffaloes Defensive Lineman

So much happened in the way of heroics over the college football weekend that you may have forgotten what happened way back on Thursday night.

That's when Deion Sanders' Colorado Buffaloes went into Atlanta and stunned Georgia Tech by blocking the would-be game-winning field goal in a 14-13 win.

The game was ugly offensively on both sides, but Colorado boasted much of the preseason about being much tougher than last year's debacle. It showed up in Game 1 – especially on defense, led by Lamont Lester Jr.

You've not heard of him. A low-level, under-the-radar transfer from Monmouth, the 6'2", 230-pound defensive lineman from New Jersey, kicked off his junior year with a performance for the ages.

He registered three sacks – all on third downs to shut down Yellow Jackets drives – and finished with 3.5 tackles for a loss overall to power the Buffs' season-opening win. He was honored as the Big 12 defensive player of the week.

Dakorien Moore, Oregon Ducks Wide Receiver

Much like Michigan, the Oregon Ducks were expected to dispatch a mid-major power relatively easily on Saturday, but that didn't go as planned.

The national champion-hopeful Ducks sweated every step of the way in a 34-27 win over Boise State in Eugene. They needed offensive heroics late in the fourth quarter after a disjointed first half.

In the end, having superior talent prevailed. No play was bigger than Dakorien Moore's stop-and-start, make-you-miss, 62-yard touchdown to put Oregon ahead for good with 8:04 left in the fourth quarter.

Moore had his moments as a sophomore a year ago, but the former top-ranked high school receiver in the nation got off to a tremendous start with six catches for 93 yards and a touchdown. On a team full of talented weapons, Moore's ability is one that stands out.

While we're talking about Big Ten receivers, we would be remiss not to mention USC true freshman Trent Mosley, who is a star right now.

He gets the nod over Penn State's Koby Howard due to the fact that the Trojans have already played two games. Mosley has shown up in a big way both times.

Coach Lincoln Riley brought in the nation's top-ranked recruiting class. Players like Luke Wafle, Kayden Dixon-Wyatt and Mark Bowman are all already special talents who are not only playing but also making spectacular plays.

Mosley – who starred throughout fall camp – is special, though. After the 5'10", 180-pound Chicago native opened the season with seven grabs for 118 yards against San Jose State, he was just as good in a win against a strong Fresno State team.

Mosley hauled in four more passes for 104 yards and scored twice in a 39-0 win. He is emerging as one of the Big Ten's top pass-catchers, regardless of class.

Mason Posa, Wisconsin Badgers Linebacker

Coach Luke Fickell is looking for any spark in a make-or-break season at Camp Randall. Wisconsin has a star-in-the-making to lead the way to, hopefully, a bowl season.

Mason Posa is a tackling machine at linebacker as a sophomore, and "Mr. Badger" is off to a huge start after a 15-tackle performance in a lopsided loss to Notre Dame at Lambeau Field on Sunday night.

One glimpse at the Irish score would have you thinking Wisconsin didn't have any reason to hope for improvement, but the game stayed close until it got out of hand late. Posa was a defensive catalyst who helped hold the Irish in check for part of the night. There won't be many offenses the Badgers face with that much potency (really, just Penn State, USC).

The 6'3", 235-pound Posa has the potential for a 100-plus tackle season after a 58-tackle, four-sack freshman campaign that saw him battle injuries and play 10 games.

Over two seasons at Tennessee, Jordan Ross showed flashes of brilliance that matched his 5-star potential but didn't quite put it all together.

He was the poster child for LSU's fast, hungry defense in a domination of Clemson on Saturday night, showcasing immense talent. The 6'5", 246-pound junior has early first-round potential on a team full of players who have star potential.

That side of the ball is why the sky is the limit in Lane Kiffin's first year on the Bayou.

Ross had four tackles, a sack and an interception that he returned for a 30-yard touchdown. Once he got the ball in his hands, the Birmingham, Alabama, native displayed the kind of athleticism that makes you look out of the side of your eye and shake your head.

He has ridiculous potential. Coordinator Blake Baker could unlock it, as LSU may have an All-American edge.

Keelon Russell, Alabama Crimson Tide Quarterback

The wait is over to see the next big thing at quarterback in Tuscaloosa.

The Keelon Russell era has begun, and even though there were some sputtering moments, the Duncanville, Texas native made certain everybody knows he has highlight-reel potential against East Carolina.

Russell took too many hits, but he got off to a roaring start in a 48-10 win, completing 18-of-30 passes for 256 yards. He also ran for 97 yards and a touchdown in the win. Those rushing yards led the Tide, too.

If you've forgotten by now, Russell was the explosive dual-threat quarterback committed to SMU who flipped to Alabama in the 2025 recruiting class. His top pass-catcher in high school was another guy on this list – Oregon's Dakorien Moore.

Alabama needs to continue developing weapons around Russell, but the sophomore can flat-out play.

Alex Golesh is known for his high-powered offense, but if he's going to have a decent first season as Auburn's head coach, the success hinges on the Tigers' defense.

Getting DJ Durkin to stick around as coordinator certainly helps, as he has some terrific playmakers on defense at all levels. In a season-opening 17-16 win over Baylor, they saved the day as the offense was awful at times behind Byrum Brown.

No play was bigger than sophomore safety Eric Winters stuffing Baylor tight end Matthew Klopfenstein on the 1-yard line in a would-be game-winning two-point conversion to seal the game.

It was a game-ball moment for Winters, who finished the game with 12 tackles (10 solo) and a forced fumble. Winters blossomed as a freshman a season ago, but he showed he's taken another step in the season opener.

He could be one of the SEC's biggest defensive stars.

articles.title: 2026 Week 2 College Football Predictions for Every Game
articles.summary: Headlined by Ohio State's trip to Texas, Week 2 of the 2026 college football season is set to bring some showdowns.
articles.body:
Headlined by Ohio State's trip to Texas, Week 2 of the 2026 college football season is set to bring some showdowns.

Texas is looking for revenge in that contest after Ohio State won last year's clash in Columbus. Either way, the winner is poised to add a very important bullet to its early College Football Playoff résumé.

Elsewhere on Saturday, Oklahoma plays at Michigan in another big nonconference rematch. Arizona heads to BYU for an intriguing Big 12 opener, as well.

Throw in Memphis' trip to Boise State, and Week 2 has a diverse range of key games throughout Saturday's slate.

No. 11 Oklahoma (1-0) at Michigan (1-0), Noon ET

Look beyond the miraculous, controversial Hail Mary for Michigan in Week 1, and the takeaway was simple: This offense looked horrendous. If the Wolverines could not create space on a respectable Western Michigan defense, can they actually handle a potentially elite Oklahoma unit? Seems doubtful.

No. 12 Alabama (1-0) at Kentucky (1-0), 3:30 p.m.

On paper, Alabama is far superior. The unknowns at Kentucky are interesting, though. New coach Will Stein is a great offensive mind, and transfer quarterback Kenny Minchey threw for 301 yards and four touchdowns in his team debut. Don't be shocked if UK becomes a thorn for Bama.

Arizona (1-0) at No. 15 BYU (1-0), 3:30 p.m.

Between a veteran roster, reliable QB in Bear Bachmeier and home-field advantage, BYU is a deserving favorite and the pick to win. However, the Cougars will be without key safety Raider Damuni due to a knee injury. One absence should not crush BYU's secondary, but that's a notable area for Arizona to attack in hopes of springing a slight upset in Provo.

Memphis (2-0) at Boise State (0-1), 6 p.m.

The winner on the blue turf should take pole position in the Group of Six's race for a CFP bid. Memphis already beat UNLV, and Boise State gained respect in a tight loss to Oregon. One issue for Memphis is four takeaways—while fantastic—atoned for a shaky day in coverage last week. Timely plays are great on defense, but Boise's offense consistently being able to move the ball is a concern.

No. 1 Ohio State (1-0) at No. 4 Texas (1-0), 7:30 p.m.

Depending on this result, Ryan Day should be fired or Arch Manning can't handle the spotlight. Take your pick. In reality, though, the only unacceptable outcome for either side would be a blowout. This margin looks minimal. Will the Texas pass-rushers win the night? Or will Ohio State's skill-position group, led by Jeremiah Smith, be enough on the road? I'll lean, not confidently, toward the latter.

Florida A&M at No. 7 Miami (1-0), Thursday, 8 p.m. ET

The result will never be a question. But after Malachi Toney struck the Heisman Trophy pose three times at Stanford, how long will the 'Canes allow him and quarterback Darian Mensah to pad their stats?

No. 23 Missouri (1-0) at Kansas (1-0), Friday, 8 p.m.

Missouri, which won the Border War meeting 42-31 last season, is a road favorite. Austin Simmons passed for 252 yards and four touchdowns in his Mizzou debut, and that offense should be the best unit on the field. Rivalries always have an element of unpredictability, but Missouri is the stronger team.

Villanova at No. 24 Louisville (0-1), Friday, 7 p.m. Prediction: Louisville 48, Villanova 10

Norfolk State at No. 25 Virginia (1-0), Friday, 7 p.m. Prediction: Virginia 49, Norfolk State 7

Richmond at North Carolina State (0-1), Friday, 7 p.m. Prediction: NC State 44, Richmond 10

Rutgers (0-1) at Boston College (0-1), Friday, 7:30 p.m. Prediction: BC 26, Rutgers 22

No. 6 Oregon (1-0) at Oklahoma State (0-1), Noon ET

I'm trying not to overreact about one game—the literal first of Eric Morris' tenure at Oklahoma State. In theory, OSU's talent and ability far outweighs what the team showed in a Week 1 loss to Tulsa. Simultaneously, it's tough to expect a real bounce-back performance when a top-ranked Oregon squad comes to Stillwater.

Prediction : Oregon 38, Oklahoma State 13

Arizona State (1-0) at No. 10 Texas A&M (1-0), Noon

Following a rout of Morgan State, Arizona State is aiming to prove it deserves more respect. Texas A&M, however, holds a two-fold advantage of an elite-level defense in a raucous home setting. There is upset potential here, but it's mild.

Prediction : Texas A&M 30, Arizona State 17

Howard at No. 5 Indiana (1-0), Noon Prediction: Indiana 59, Howard 7

articles.title: Anthony Martial se ofrece al Málaga
articles.standfirst: El club valora el nombre pese a su reciente historial
articles.summary: El club valora el nombre pese a su reciente historial
articles.body: El Málaga CF busca soluciones para uno de sus grandes problemas en este inicio de temporada: el gol. El equipo de Juanfran Funes sólo ha marcado un tanto en las cuatro primeras jornadas de LaLiga y llegó desde el punto de penalti. Una necesidad que se ha acentuado tras la lesión de larga duración de Julen Lobete. Con el mercado cerrado, la dirección deportiva blanquiazul mira hacia los agentes libres. Y uno de los nombres que ha aparecido sobre la mesa es el de Anthony Martial. El francés ha sido ofrecido al Málaga y el club estudia seriamente su incorporación, tal y como adelantó Matteo Moretto. Su polivalencia es uno de los puntos a favor. Martial puede jugar tanto en banda como en la punta del ataque, dos posiciones en las que el conjunto de Martiricos necesita mejorar sus prestaciones. Según ha podido saber Radio MARCA Málaga, el jugador ve con buenos ojos la posibilidad de llegar a La Rosaleda. Martial quiere jugar esta temporada en LaLiga y estaría dispuesto a realizar un importante esfuerzo económico para facilitar la operación. Sin embargo, el Málaga tendrá competencia, ya que otros clubes también siguen su situación. El francés se encuentra sin equipo después de su última experiencia en el CF Monterrey, donde disputó 20 partidos, marcó un gol y repartió tres asistencias. Antes, en el AEK de Atenas, firmó nueve tantos en 24 encuentros. Su gran explosión llegó en Francia, especialmente en el AS Mónaco, antes de que el Manchester United pagara unos 50 millones de euros por él en 2015. Ese mismo año recibió el Golden Boy. Martial también conoce el fútbol español tras su paso por el Sevilla, donde disputó doce encuentros. Ahora, libre y con el deseo de jugar en España, su nombre aparece como una de las opciones que valora el Málaga para tratar de solucionar su preocupante falta de gol.

articles.title: Rodri se disculpa con Gayà tras el "son malísimos" referido al Valencia
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Barcelona llamó al capitán blanquinegro para que hiciera extensivas las disculpas al resto del vestuario
articles.summary: El jugador del Barcelona llamó al capitán blanquinegro para que hiciera extensivas las disculpas al resto del vestuario
articles.body: Rodri Hernández se ha puesto en contacto con José Luis Gayà para disculparse por las palabras que pronunció durante el partido entre Valencia y Barcelona en Mestalla y que fueron captadas por las cámaras de El Día Después de Movistar+. La información, adelantada por El Partit de la 1 de À Punt, revela que el centrocampista azulgrana llamó personalmente al capitán valencianista para disculparse y explicarle el contexto de aquella conversación y trasladarle que nunca tuvo intención de menospreciar al conjunto valencianista. El episodio se produjo durante la contundente victoria del Barcelona por 0-5 en Mestalla. Rodri, que había sido sustituido en la segunda mitad, mantenía una conversación informal en el banquillo con Pau Cubarsí cuando las cámaras recogieron varios comentarios sobre el rendimiento del Valencia. En las imágenes difundidas se puede leer en los labios del internacional español afirmar: “Muy flojos, son muy flojos estos, ¿eh?. Muy flojos, tío” y, posteriormente, insistir: “Son muy malos, tío, son malísimos”. En otro momento de la charla preguntó a Cubarsí cómo había terminado el Valencia la temporada anterior y mostró sorpresa al conocer que el equipo había acabado cerca de las plazas europeas. En un momento, Rodri se cube la boca con una toalla que tiene al cuello, pero la conversación ya la habían captado las cámaras. Según ha podido confirmar MARCA, Rodri explicó a Gayà que aquellas manifestaciones se produjeron en un contexto privado y distendido, junto a un compañero de equipo, sin intención de faltar al respeto a los futbolistas valencianistas ni de cuestionar públicamente su nivel. El mediocentro le pidió, además, que su mensaje fuera trasladado al resto del vestuario del Valencia para evitar malentendidos y zanjar cualquier malestar derivado de la difusión de las imágenes. El capitán del Valencia aceptó las disculpas, pero sí le dejó claro que se había equivocado. La polémica adquirió una gran repercusión en las horas posteriores a la emisión del programa, especialmente por tratarse de un futbolista de la ascendencia de Rodri, capitán de la selección española y uno de los referentes del Barcelona. Además, el vídeo superó el millón de reproducciones en el perfil de Movistar + en la red social X antes de ser borrado. Según el entorno del futbolista, Rodri quedó afectado por la interpretación pública de unas palabras que nunca pensó que trascenderían fuera del ámbito interno del partido.

articles.title: Giggs cuenta a qué futbolista se hubiera llevado del Manchester United Guardiola a su City
articles.standfirst: El mítico futbolista galés le preguntó al técnico español a qué red devil se llevaría a su equipo durante una cena organizada por Sir Alex Ferguson poco después de llegar al club cityzen
articles.summary: El mítico futbolista galés le preguntó al técnico español a qué red devil se llevaría a su equipo durante una cena organizada por Sir Alex Ferguson poco después de llegar al club cityzen
articles.body: ¿De Gea? ¿Luke Shaw?" Ninguno de estas dos futbolistas propuestos por Ryan Gyggs fueron admitidas por Pep Guardiola para llevárselas de Old Trafford a su Manchester City. Entonces ¿Quién puede ser? Durante la última entrega de The Debrief, el espacio presentado por Rio Ferdinand, Ryan Giggs, una de las grandes leyendas del Manchester United, desveló una anécdota de hace "ocho o nueve años" durante una cena que compartió con Sir Alex Ferguson y Guardiola, en la que el entrenador del Manchester City no ocultó su admiración por un futbolista muy concreto del United. Según explicó el galés, el técnico catalán llegó a reconocer que, si hubiera tenido la oportunidad, se habría llevado a este delantero del United a su equipo "mañana mismo". Dicha confesión que sorprendió a Ferdinand y sirve, además, para dimensionar el talento que todavía se le atribuye al internacional inglés pese a sus altibajos recientes. ¿Ya sabes quién es? Marcus Rashford, un futbolista que en las últimas temporadas ha tenido muchos altibajos, pero quizás, tras su paso por el Barcelona, y su regreso a Old Trafford de la mano de Michael Carrick, esté en el camino de volver a ser el que fue. Giggs, que conoce mejor que nadie la presión de triunfar en Old Trafford, recordó que él mismo vivió momentos complicados durante su carrera, llegando incluso a recibir críticas y pitidos de los aficionados. Desde esa experiencia personal, el galés defendió que Rashford todavía tiene margen para reconstruir su relación con la grada, aunque dejó claro que el camino pasa principalmente por sus actuaciones sobre el terreno de juego. Durante la charla, Ferdinand y Giggs coincidieron en que el delantero debe volver a centrarse en los aspectos básicos que siempre distinguieron a los grandes jugadores del United: esfuerzo, compromiso y regularidad. El exextremo insistió especialmente en la importancia del trabajo sin balón y de mantener una actitud competitiva constante, elementos que históricamente han marcado la diferencia para los futbolistas que triunfan en el club. Lejos de dar por perdido al atacante, Giggs se mostró optimista sobre sus opciones de recuperar su mejor versión. El exinternacional galés entiende que Rashford aún está a tiempo de revertir la situación y volver a convertirse en uno de los referentes de Old Trafford. El mensaje final fue claro: para reconquistar a los seguidores del Manchester United no hacen falta discursos, sino rendimiento, trabajo y actuaciones decisivas cada fin de semana.

articles.title: Iowa football opponent preview: ISU players to watch for
articles.summary: The Cyclones bring a brand-new roster to town this weekend. Despite that, there's still some real talent for Iowa football to contend with.
articles.body:
The annual Cy-Hawk football game is just a few days away. In the past, this game has always brought a sense of familiarity between the two rivals, as players would appear in three or four of these games during their careers. That won't be the case this season for the visiting team.

Iowa State underwent a massive program shakeup this offseason. Longtime head coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State , bringing many of his elite players with him. With Campbell, quarterback Rocco Becht , and many others now in Happy Valley, the Cyclones' roster looks very different from last season.

New head coach Jimmy Rogers came over from Washington State and attacked the transfer portal ferociously. The result is a roster that many Hawkeye fans are unfamiliar with. But, it's a roster that is capable of winning this game on the right day.

If Iowa wants to avoid a third-straight Cy-Hawk defeat, these are the players they'll need to keep an eye on:

2026 stats: 8-16, 184 yards, 4 total TDs (2 passing, 2 rushing)

The Cyclones' newest quarterback was pretty good in his Iowa State debut. The former Arkansas State signal-caller accounted for four total touchdowns in a season-opening 38-10 win over Southeast Missouri State. Jaylen Raynor hit some big plays through the air, but struggled with consistency.

The 6-foot-1, 208-pound quarterback is dangerous with his legs, but prone to mistakes (28 career interceptions). Iowa will have to keep him in the pocket on Saturday.

Aiden Flora is one of the few holdovers from last year's roster. He started at running back in Week 1 and led the team in rushing yards. Iowa State will use him, Raynor, and Cameron Pettaway in the run game, which the Hawkeyes will need to account for. Flora also returns punts for the Cyclones.

The 6-foot, 195-pound back had three returns for 33 yards last weekend. This will be a good test for Iowa 's unproven defensive line.

Isaac Terrell was a man among boys in Iowa State's season opener. The 6-foot-2, 255-pound Washington State transfer lived in the backfield, racking up three sacks and forcing a fumble. He had seven sacks with the Cougars a year ago and picked right back up where he left off in Week 1. Iowa's offensive line is stout, but they'll be challenged by Terrell and the Cyclones' defensive line in this game.

Sullivan Schlimgen is another Washington State transfer who followed his coach to Ames. The 6-foot-1, 220-pound linebacker led the Cyclones in tackles last weekend and also found his way to the quarterback for a sack. He had 49 total tackles with the Cougars in 2025 and should build on that in 2026.

The Hawkeyes will be looking to establish the ground game on Saturday. They'll have to contend with Schlimgen at the second level.

2026 stats: 1-for-1 FG (33-yard make), 5-for-5 extra points

Iowa fans are extremely familiar with Konrardy. The 6-foot-1 kicker has booted the game-winning field goal in each of the past two Cy-Hawk games. In 2024, he nailed a 54-yard field goal with six seconds left to play for the win in Iowa City. Last season, he made another 54-yarder with just under two minutes left to play to seal the win in Ames. The best way for Iowa to avoid Konrardy is to ensure the game doesn't come down to his leg again.

articles.title: French FA to withdraw support to FIFA President Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: The French Football Federation (FFF) are expected to announce in the coming hours that they are withdrawing their support for outgoing FIFA president Gianni...
articles.body:
The French Football Federation (FFF) are expected to announce in the coming hours that they are withdrawing their support for outgoing FIFA president Gianni Infantino, according to reports from Agence France-Presse .

Whilst an executive committee meeting of the federation is due to take place this Thursday to decide on the association's position regarding the Italian-Swiss leader, who is seeking a further term at the helm of FIFA, their decision is expected this afternoon.

And barring any exceptional turn of events, the FFF will likely follow the lead set by Sweden , Scotland , Italy and Belgium , as well as the Hungarian Sandor Csanyi, one of the eight vice-presidents of the FIFA Council, all of whom have distanced themselves from Infantino.

This shift follows, in particular, the Federation's complete disagreement with the latter's now-abandoned plan to privatise the World Cup.

Whilst he remains, for the time being, the sole candidate to succeed himself, Infantino is likely to find out the identity of his rival(s) very soon, with the presidential election due to take place on 18th March 2027 in Rabat.

articles.title: Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Paul Merson gives his verdict on Arsenal's Champions League hopes in his latest column; Sky Sports pundit believes Gunners needed more than Kai Havertz up front; Follow Napoli vs Arsenal on the Sky Sports app with our dedicated match commentary from 6.30pm on Wednesday
articles.body:
They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient.

If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League.

I'm a big fan of Kai Havertz. He does a lot of work and he's what I call a good footballer. He works hard and makes the right decisions. I just think he's not going to score 20 goals in a season. To take them to the Premier League title, there's no doubt about it, he's a top-drawer player.

The other thing I look at is when Arsenal go and play against Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, teams like that in the Champions League latter stages, the centre-halves and the full-backs, getting up in the morning and going to their team talk and saying to one of the other players, "Didn't sleep very well last night, a bit worried about who I'm playing against".

I don't see that for Arsenal. Maybe Bukayo Saka for the left-back, but they haven't got that X factor.

I think that's what they found out in the final last year. Arsenal had no pace getting forward, and PSG just squeezed the game up and didn't let Arsenal out of their half. That would be the worry.

They had been so close to winning the Premier League and then they got over the line, I wouldn't say comfortably, but they've kicked on again.

They've got some good players. I think they could have gone on again and bought a real, real superstar. But their squad is immense. It's so solid.

It's so hard just to get a shot off against them, let alone score a goal. Chelsea went there with one of the best, if not the best, front threes in the Premier League.

They scored after 77 seconds, but I can't remember them ever looking like they'd score another goal after that. So that just shows you how dominant Arsenal are at the moment.

It's important you start well in the Champions League. When the tournament changed to this format, teams struggled. They had eight games, they thought they'd win enough and get through. Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain struggled at times to get through.

And then last year, everybody tried to get their wins under their belt very, very quickly. This is an important game tonight. They'll want to keep the momentum going.

If you'd said to me a year or two ago, Napoli away, I'd have said it was a hard game. But Chelsea went there in Europe and beat them and they hadn't been beaten for a long time at home. So they're beatable and I don't expect Arsenal to lose.

articles.title: Stassin: "Cuando me hablaron del proyecto no lo pensé dos veces"
articles.standfirst: El delantero belga, que se estrenó con gol ante el Espanyol, llega al Sevilla cedido por el Saint-Éttienne
articles.summary: El delantero belga, que se estrenó con gol ante el Espanyol, llega al Sevilla cedido por el Saint-Éttienne
articles.body: Este miércoles, Lucas Stassin ha sido presentado como nuevo futbolista del Sevilla junto con Félix Correia y Youssouf Fofana. "Ha sido una semana muy rápida porque hemos llegado todos en el último minuto del mercado de fichajes, pero ya hemos podido jugar, nos sentimos muy bien en el equipo y el grupo nos ha acogido muy bien", comenzó el delantero belga, que llega al Sevilla cedido del Saint-Éttienne y ya debutó con gol en el último partido ante el Espanyol. Debut con gol. "La verdad es que siempre es algo magnífico poder marcar, y más hacerlo en el primer partido. Me hubiese gustado conseguir los tres puntos, que hubiese sido algo mucho mejor, pero nos fuimos con un punto y espero continuar de esta manera y seguir marcando en los próximos partidos". ¿Por qué el Sevilla? "Para mí es una gran oportunidad, porque sabemos todo lo que ha conseguido el Sevilla, el club que es. Sinceramente, me sentí muy contento cuando me hablaron del proyecto porque no tuve que pensarlo dos veces. Me dieron mucha confianza y así lo decidí". Adaptación. "Para mí es la primera vez que juego en España, con lo cual voy a intentar adaptarme lo más rápido posible al vestuario y a los compañeros. Voy a intentar aprender el idioma. Es un nuevo campeonato para mí, así que voy a intentar dar el máximo para ayudar al equipo. He tenido una buena adaptación en los últimos días". Objetivos. "Tenemos que ser muy competitivos, intentar pensar en cada partido individualmente. Somos un equipo, somos una familia, como dice el entrenador, y tenemos que intentar jugar bien al fútbol, intentar ganar los partidos, tener muchas ganas y veremos al final qué hemos conseguido y qué no. Quiero que podamos volver a poner al club donde se merece". Viaje junto a Correia. "Ya me dijeron que iba a ir en el mismo vuelo que yo, entonces hicimos todo juntos, las visitas médicas, etc. Estuvo bien, ya hemos creado un pequeño vínculo en ese pequeño viaje". Cifra goleadora. "Voy a intentar marcar los máximos goles posibles, pensar en cada partido y marcar goles importantes sobre todo para conseguir los tres puntos, para mí eso es lo más importante, ayudar al equipo y a los compañeros. Sabemos que el 9 tiene que marcar, pero también tiene que participar en el juego. Y voy a intentar marcar al máximo y conseguir los máximos puntos". Recomendación de compañeros. "Algunos amigos belgas que ya han pasado por este club me dijeron que era magnífico. Sinceramente, yo ya tenía simpatía por este club por ciertos amigos. Me han acogido muy bien, ya me dijeron que iría todo genial y que sería un campeonato y una liga muy buena para mí. Veo mucha calidad en el vestuario y veremos cómo va a funcionar todo, pero sí, me hablaron muy bien de este equipo". Dos delanteros. "Conozco a Robbie porque coincidimos en el Anderlecht. Me siento muy bien jugando con tres delanteros o con dos. Luego va a ser el entrenador el que decida en función de cada partido, pero en cualquier caso puedo jugar yo solo, con dos o con tres delanteros Ya veremos cómo decide el entrenador".

articles.title: 10th Mountain Division honored with helmet patch for Army football home opener
articles.summary: The 10th Mountain Division at Fort Drum was honored during the Army football team's home opener last weekend.
articles.body:
WEST POINT, N.Y. (WWTI) - The 10th Mountain Division at Fort Drum was honored during the Army football team's home opener last weekend.

The division had its patch worn on the back of the Black Knights' helmets during the Sept. 5 season opener against Bryant.

For the whole season, Army players will wear division patches on the backs of their helmets to recognize the history, accomplishments and continued service of Army divisions.

The West Point campus and Fort Drum do share connections, as Assistant professor and personnel officer in the Department of History and War Studies at West Point Lt. Col. Paul Belmont spent much of his career with the division.

Belmont returned to Fort Drum after a tour at West Point to do his key development time as a major with 1st and 3rd Brigades, and it is truly what he calls 'home.'

"I have owned two homes in Watertown, I love North Country," said Belmont, who has rented those homes to many 10th Mountain Soldiers. "I loved being a Knight Hawk, a Spartan and a Warrior. I went back to Iraq with my GO and back to Afghanistan as an Iron Major."

The football team has honored Fort Drum before, as it wore white uniforms in the Black Knights' 14-13 win in December 2017 over the rival United States Naval Academy.

Army cruised past Bryant for a 59-3 victory on Sept 5.
